executive_summary:
Chairman ratification e38df53f (2026-09-14): freeze the open harness backlog (feedback row 58cc4231: 29 SD keys + 109 QF ids) as the finish line, check every NEW item for criticality before filing, route non-critical items to the existing harness_backlog channel instead of creating a QF/SD, and surface ratification 3c4a6781 (the clean-slate test venture) to the chairman once the baseline reaches zero. The rule and its four criteria (breaks a venture stage or the coming test venture, loses data, stops the fleet working, or is a security risk) are already encoded in CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE_ADAM.md/CLAUDE_COORDINATOR.md prose (PR #8968) -- what does not exist is enforcement in code, so today the rule binds only the seats that happen to read and follow it. This SD makes the actual filing TOOLS carry the check, so it binds every filer including automated generators that never read a CLAUDE.md file. Measured 2026-09-14: SD inflow (113/7d) tracks completions (99/7d) closely enough that an unenforced finish line never arrives.

EXEC-phase code research (this PRD) found the real call-site surface is LARGER than the SD's own originating scope text names: 2 call sites the SD's scope text explicitly names (create-quick-fix.js's insert, leo-create-sd.js's createSD() choke) PLUS 2 more this PRD's own investigation found that bypass both of those entirely -- lib/eva/quality-findings/sd-generator.js's insertDraftRemediationSd() (direct strategic_directives_v2 insert) and mintVentureQuickFix() (direct quick_fixes insert). All 4 are in scope; a gate that only covers 2 of the 4 real creation paths would be exactly the 'printed discriminator, not an enforced gate' failure this ratification exists to close.

functional_requirements.title: Criticality verdict gate on create-quick-fix.js, warn-first via a leo_feature_flags flag
functional_requirements.description: Add a `--criticality <critical|later>` flag (values case-insensitive, normalized) and a `--criticality-reason "<one-line>"` flag to scripts/create-quick-fix.js's CLI arg parsing (NOT `--reason`, which is already an alias for `--force-claim-reason` at line ~968 -- reusing it would silently corrupt an unrelated field). The gate check runs early, right after the existing type/severity validation and normalization completes (after line 231) and BEFORE the EVA pre-check (line 233) and dedup scans (lines 265-439), so a 'later' verdict short-circuits before any expensive Supabase round-trips. Read a `QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE` row from `leo_feature_flags` (is_enabled boolean, default/missing-row-safe FALSE) using the exact read pattern already established in lib/eva/stage-execution-worker.js (~line 3209-3238: select is_enabled, maybeSingle, default to false on any error/absent row -- fail toward NOT blocking yet). When the flag is OFF (the initial release state): a missing --criticality is logged as `console.warn('... would have REFUSED filing (no --criticality) ... but QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE is not enabled -- filing anyway.')`, matching the exact structured log-line convention from stage-execution-worker.js, and the QF is filed normally. When the flag is ON (the later, enforced release): a missing --criticality causes the tool to exit non-zero with a message naming all four criticality criteria verbatim (breaks a venture stage or the coming test venture / loses data / stops the fleet working / is a security risk) and does NOT file anything. In both flag states, when --criticality IS supplied: 'critical' proceeds to the normal insert with `metadata.criticality='critical'` and `metadata.criticality_reason` stamped on the row; 'later' NEVER reaches the quick_fixes insert -- it routes per FR-3 instead.
acceptance_criteria: With QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE OFF (or the row absent) and no --criticality flag: the QF still files (unchanged current behavior), but a distinguishable warning is printed naming the flag.
With QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE ON and no --criticality flag: the process exits non-zero, no quick_fixes row is created, and the four criticality criteria appear verbatim in the printed message.

With --criticality critical (any flag state): the quick_fixes row is created with metadata.criticality='critical' and metadata.criticality_reason set from --criticality-reason (empty string if omitted, never a crash).

With --criticality later (any flag state): NO quick_fixes row is created; a unit test confirms the insert code path (the redraw-on-collision loop around line 480-507) is never reached, by asserting the mocked supabase client's quick_fixes.insert was never called.

--criticality is normalized case-insensitively ('Critical', 'LATER', etc. all accepted); an unrecognized value (neither critical nor later) is treated the same as a MISSING verdict (never silently defaults to 'critical').

functional_requirements.title: Criticality verdict gate at the createSD() choke point, covering all 8 SD-creation CLI lanes AND the existing non-CLI programmatic callers that already reach it
functional_requirements.description:
Add `options.criticality`/`options.criticalityReason` destructuring to createSD() in lib/sd-creation/pipeline.js (near its existing sdKey fail-fast check, ~line 661-662, alongside the ~25 other destructured options at lines 594-651) -- this single choke point is already the point EVERY one of the 8 leo-create-sd.js CLI lanes (--from-uat, --from-learn, --from-feedback, --from-roadmap-item, --from-qf, --from-proposal family [scripts/modules/leo-create-sd/proposal-lanes.js], --from-plan, --child, and the direct <source> <type> "<title>" lane [scripts/modules/leo-create-sd/direct-lane.js]) converges through (confirmed: uat.js:61, roadmap-item.js:108, qf.js:239, plan.js:363, learn.js:45, feedback.js:162, child.js:166, direct-lane.js:378, proposal-lanes.js:467 all call it), so gating here covers every CLI lane in one place rather than 8 separate call sites. Same flag-read pattern as FR-1 but its own flag key, `SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE`, read once per createSD() call. scripts/leo-create-sd.js's own argument parsing for each of the 8 lanes needs a `--criticality`/`--criticality-reason` flag threaded through to whichever options object each lane builds before calling createSD() -- reuse the SAME flag names as FR-1's QF gate for filer-facing consistency, even though the underlying leo_feature_flags rows are separate (a QF and an SD gate should be independently promotable to enforced, since their filer populations and volumes differ, per FR-1/FR-2's own measured 113 SD vs 256 QF/7d volumes).

ADDITIONAL, VALIDATION-FOUND REQUIREMENT: 4 EXISTING programmatic (non-CLI) callers already call createSD() directly and supply no criticality today -- action-executor.js:138, convergence-remediation-writers.js:65, eva-master-scheduler.js:749, class-escalation.js:140. These already reach FR-2's gate (they are not a bypass), but once SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE flips to true they would each start failing (no criticality supplied) unless given an explicit default NOW, in this same SD, alongside the gate itself -- shipping the gate without this would silently break 4 live automated SD-filing flows the moment the flag is later enabled. Add `criticality: 'later'` directly to each of these 4 call sites' options object (matching the same 'generators default to later, never critical' policy FR-4 applies to the true bypass paths) -- a mechanical, one-line addition per site, not a design change to any of the 4 files' own logic.
acceptance_criteria: createSD() reads SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE via the same fail-safe pattern as FR-1 (missing row/read error -> not enabled, never a crash, never silently enforced-by-default).

At least 2 of the 8 CLI lanes (the direct lane and one other, e.g. --from-qf) are updated to accept and thread through --criticality/--criticality-reason -- a unit test for each confirms the flag reaches createSD()'s options object unchanged.

With SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE ON and no criticality option: createSD() returns an error result (not a thrown exception -- matching this function's existing error-return convention, e.g. the sdKey fail-fast precedent) naming the four criteria, and no strategic_directives_v2 row is inserted.
With criticality:'later': no strategic_directives_v2 insert occurs (a unit test confirms the mocked insert is never called), and control passes to FR-3's routing instead.
With criticality:'critical': the insert proceeds with metadata.criticality/metadata.criticality_reason stamped on the created row.

Each of the 4 named programmatic callers (action-executor.js:138, convergence-remediation-writers.js:65, eva-master-scheduler.js:749, class-escalation.js:140) is confirmed, by grep or a unit test reading the actual call-site source, to pass criticality:'later' explicitly in its createSD() call -- so flipping SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE to true cannot break any of these 4 existing flows.

functional_requirements.title: 'later' verdict routes to the existing harness_backlog feedback channel via emitFeedback, never a new table
functional_requirements.description: When either gate (FR-1 or FR-2) resolves a 'later' verdict, call `emitFeedback` (imported directly from lib/governance/emit-feedback.js -- NOT scripts/log-harness-bug.js, which is a CLI-only wrapper around the same function, confirmed via its own header comment and its findPossiblePriorFix export already being the one piece of that file safe to import) with `{ supabase, title, description, category: 'harness_backlog', severity: 'medium', source_type: 'manual_feedback', metadata: { logged_via: '<create-quick-fix.js|leo-create-sd.js>', criticality_reason, deferred_from: '<the title/description that would have been filed>' } }`. Print the resulting feedback row id and 'routed to harness_backlog (feedback id: <id>)' so the filer sees where the item went, matching the SD's own success-criteria wording. emitFeedback's own sha256-based dedup (title+description+dedup_key) means a filer re-running the identical later-routed item twice does not create duplicate feedback rows -- rely on this existing behavior rather than re-implementing dedup.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test stubs emitFeedback and confirms it is called with category:'harness_backlog' exactly once when FR-1's gate resolves 'later', with the QF's title/description/criticality_reason present in the call.
A unit test confirms the same for FR-2's SD gate.
The printed output on a 'later' routing names the created feedback row id and says where the item went (grep-testable exact substring, e.g. 'routed to harness_backlog').
No new database table or column beyond the existing feedback.metadata JSONB is introduced.

functional_requirements.title: Generator/automated bypass paths that never reach createSD()/create-quick-fix.js default to 'later', never 'critical' -- including the largest-volume bypass (lifecycle-sd-bridge.js)
functional_requirements.description:
VALIDATION's LEAD-phase review measured live 30-day SD-creation volume by source and found the SD's originally-scoped bypass (sd-generator.js, ~6 SDs/30d) is NOT the largest one: lib/eva/lifecycle-sd-bridge.js accounts for ~30 SDs/30d (5x larger) and was not named in this SD's own originating scope text. All direct-insert bypass paths, in descending measured volume:
(a) lib/eva/lifecycle-sd-bridge.js's insertSDIdempotent() (line 521) -- the SHARED insert helper most call sites in this file already funnel through (confirmed: it already stamps `row.metadata.sourced_by = 'lifecycle-sd-bridge'`, guarded by `if (row.metadata && row.metadata.sourced_by === undefined)` at line 525-527 -- NOT unconditional, a guard this SD's own addition mirrors -- following the exact precedent set by SD-LEO-INFRA-DISPATCH-AUTH-AUTO-AUTHORIZE-001-B FR-4's own comment: 'stamp the mint-path provenance signal here, in the one shared insert helper, so every call site in this file is covered uniformly rather than patched piecemeal'). Add the identical pattern: `if (row.metadata && row.metadata.criticality === undefined) { row.metadata.criticality = 'later'; row.metadata.criticality_reason = 'auto-generated by lifecycle-sd-bridge, unsupervised -- routed later by default per SD-LEO-INFRA-FILING-TOOLS-ENFORCE-001 FR-4'; }` immediately alongside the existing sourced_by stamp -- one shared helper, one addition, covers most call sites in the file. CONFIRMED EXCEPTION (VALIDATION's 2nd-round review): line 1487 is a SEPARATE, inline `strategic_directives_v2` insert on the venture-expansion path that does NOT call insertSDIdempotent() -- measured 0 SDs in 30d/180d/all-time (dormant, not currently leaking). Give it the same one-line stamp directly on its own insert object as a matter of completeness, but it is not a live-volume risk if EXEC time runs short.
(b) lib/eva/quality-findings/sd-generator.js's insertDraftRemediationSd() (line 707, called from generateRemediationSdsForVenture() at line 790) does a DIRECT `.from('strategic_directives_v2').insert(...)` (lines 737-759) that bypasses createSD() entirely, by this module's own documented design (header comment: 'bypasses leo-create-sd.js for high-volume venture-scoped batching'). Same stamp: hardcode `metadata.criticality: 'later'` directly into the insert object.
(c) lib/eva/quality-findings/sd-generator.js's mintVentureQuickFix() (line 684, its own direct `.from('quick_fixes').insert()` at lines 689-702) -- the QF-side equivalent of (b). Same treatment.
(d) generateRemediationSD()/buildCreateSdArgs() (sd-generator.js line 148/195) spawns the leo-create-sd.js CLI's direct lane -- this DOES reach createSD() via FR-2's choke point (not a bypass), so it just needs `--criticality later` appended to the spawned args by default unless the caller explicitly supplies a verdict.
Any further static direct-SD-insert call sites found during EXEC (e.g. lib/eva/convergence-remediation-writers.js has both a createSD()-based path, covered by FR-2, and is worth a final grep sweep for any OTHER direct-insert site) should receive the same stamp; if a live-volume check shows near-zero traffic, note it in the retrospective as a deliberately deferred low-priority stamp rather than silently skipping it unrecorded.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test confirms insertSDIdempotent() stamps metadata.criticality='later' (never overwriting an already-set value) on every row it inserts, mirroring its existing sourced_by-stamping test coverage if any exists.
A unit test confirms generateRemediationSD()'s spawned CLI args include `--criticality later` when its caller supplies no explicit verdict.
A unit test confirms insertDraftRemediationSd()'s insert object always carries metadata.criticality='later' (never 'critical', never absent).
A unit test confirms mintVentureQuickFix()'s insert object always carries metadata.criticality='later'.

No generator/bridge path can produce metadata.criticality='critical' without an explicit, traceable override from its caller (grep-testable: the literal string 'critical' as a criticality value appears nowhere in lifecycle-sd-bridge.js's or sd-generator.js's own source, only 'later').

functional_requirements.title: BASELINE_REMAINING reader: counts non-terminal baseline ids, verifying the ORIGINAL historical sha256 directly (algorithm recovered and confirmed, read-only)
functional_requirements.description:
New script, scripts/baseline-remaining.mjs. Reads feedback row 58cc4231-1710-4693-97ff-723e3685a2e4 (query by id, not title -- the title string is display text and could theoretically change; find it once by title/category='chairman_directive' at first-run time if the literal UUID ever needs re-resolving, but hardcode the confirmed UUID as the primary lookup). Extracts metadata.baseline.sd_keys (29 strings) and metadata.baseline.qf_ids (109 strings). Queries strategic_directives_v2/quick_fixes for the current status of exactly those ids, counts how many are NON-terminal (status not in the completed/cancelled set already established by this SD's own 'finish_line' definition: 'every sd_key and qf_id in baseline reaches completed or cancelled', reusing metadata.open_definition's exact status sets already stored on the same row rather than re-deriving them), and prints `BASELINE_REMAINING sd=<N> qf=<M>`.

CORRECTED from an earlier draft of this PRD, per VALIDATION's LEAD-phase review: the original freeze algorithm IS recoverable and IS reproducible -- VALIDATION found the actual freeze scripts on disk (`.artifacts/adam-freeze-baseline.mjs`, `.artifacts/adam-freeze-baseline-v2.mjs`, untracked but present) and confirmed the exact algorithm: `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify({ sdKeys: metadata.baseline.sd_keys, qfIds: metadata.baseline.qf_ids })).digest('hex')` -- note the CAMELCASE object keys (`sdKeys`/`qfIds`) in the JSON.stringify input, distinct from the snake_case (`sd_keys`/`qf_ids`) the VALUES are stored under in metadata.baseline; this key-name mismatch (not ordering, sorting, or serialization, all of which an earlier draft tried) is exactly why 12 earlier attempts at reproduction failed. Independently re-verified against BOTH the live 58cc4231 row (sha256 956e8734...d557, MATCH) and the prior superseded freeze row referenced in its own metadata.supersedes (f4b016d8, sha256 8c18dac3...af1f, MATCH) -- two independent (input, output) pairs confirming the algorithm, not one lucky match.

The reader therefore implements the SD's own literal text directly: recompute `sha256(JSON.stringify({ sdKeys: b.sd_keys, qfIds: b.qf_ids }))` from the CURRENT metadata.baseline content and compare against the stored metadata.sha256; on mismatch, fail loud (non-zero exit, explicit error naming both hashes) rather than silently proceeding. This is READ-ONLY -- no write to the feedback row of any kind. (An earlier draft of this PRD proposed writing a new checkpoint field to this row; VALIDATION separately found that write would be illegal regardless -- database/chairman-gated/20260907_feedback_immutability_trigger.sql stages triggers rejecting ANY update to the feedback table, including service_role. Confirming the original hash IS reproducible makes this moot, but the write-illegality is worth recording here so no future revision of this script reintroduces an update attempt.)
acceptance_criteria: Running the script against the real feedback row prints BASELINE_REMAINING sd=<N> qf=<M> where N/M are independently confirmed correct by a direct SELECT COUNT over the same id lists filtered to non-terminal status.

The script recomputes sha256(JSON.stringify({sdKeys, qfIds})) from the live row's current metadata.baseline content and confirms it equals the stored metadata.sha256 -- a unit test with a known (sdKeys, qfIds, expected_hash) fixture (the two pairs found during PLAN-phase research, 58cc4231 and f4b016d8, both usable as literal test fixtures) proves the algorithm is implemented correctly, not merely that it happens to match once.

A test that mutates a copy of the id lists (simulating tampering) confirms the script detects the mismatch against the KNOWN-correct algorithm and fails loud (non-zero exit, explicit error message naming both the computed and stored hash) rather than silently proceeding.
The script never calls .update()/.upsert() against the feedback table -- grep-confirmed read-only, consistent with the table's immutability trigger.

functional_requirements.title: Finish-line surfacing: exactly one chairman decision row when BASELINE_REMAINING reaches sd=0 qf=0, idempotent
functional_requirements.description: When scripts/baseline-remaining.mjs computes sd=0 AND qf=0, call `recordPendingDecision` (imported from lib/chairman/record-pending-decision.mjs, the confirmed canonical helper for chairman_decisions inserts -- NOT a hand-rolled .from('chairman_decisions').insert()) with a distinct, greppable `decisionType` (e.g. `'harness_baseline_finish_line'`) so idempotency can be checked by querying chairman_decisions for an existing row with that exact decision_type before calling recordPendingDecision again -- if one already exists, print a no-op message and take no further action (this is the 'a second run creates none' requirement). title/context/recommendation reference ratification 3c4a6781 (the clean-slate test venture decision) by name and summarize that the harness backlog baseline (feedback 58cc4231) has reached zero remaining items. blocking:true (a real decision the chairman needs to act on, not an FYI).
acceptance_criteria: A unit test with sd=0/qf=0 and no existing chairman_decisions row of decisionType='harness_baseline_finish_line' confirms recordPendingDecision is called exactly once with blocking:true and a title/context referencing 3c4a6781.
A unit test with sd=0/qf=0 and an EXISTING row of that decisionType confirms recordPendingDecision is NOT called again, and the script prints a no-op/already-surfaced message.
A unit test with sd>0 or qf>0 confirms recordPendingDecision is never called.

technical_requirements.title: No schema migration
technical_requirements.description: All new state lives in existing metadata JSONB columns (quick_fixes.metadata, strategic_directives_v2.metadata, feedback.metadata) and a new metadata key on the existing baseline feedback row. No new tables, no new columns via migration -- matching the SD's own explicit out-of-scope boundary.

technical_requirements.title: Flag-governance rows are new leo_feature_flags entries, registered via a migration (INSERT only, matching the precedent migrations)
technical_requirements.description: QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE and SD_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE are new rows in leo_feature_flags, is_enabled=false at creation (warn-first release), following the exact precedent shape of LEO_SYNTHETIC_ACTOR_FENCE_ENFORCE/PATH_INTEGRITY_EXIT_GATE_ENFORCE (database/migrations/20260823_register_path_integrity_flags.sql is the template migration to follow) -- including populated enablement_criteria/gates_what description fields, not bare inserts.

technical_requirements.title: SD_CREATE_VIA_SKILL is a Bash-tool PreToolUse hook gate only, not a code-level check -- irrelevant to this SD's enforcement point
technical_requirements.description: Confirmed: scripts/hooks/pre-tool-enforce.cjs's ENFORCEMENT 9 intercepts direct `node .../leo-create-sd.js` invocations issued via Claude Code's own Bash tool; it does NOT fire on child_process.spawn() calls made by already-running application code (sd-generator.js's own spawn, clockwork loop scripts, etc.). This SD's gates live inside createSD()/create-quick-fix.js's own logic specifically because that is the only place unconditionally reached by every caller, human or programmatic.

technical_requirements.title: Out of scope, explicitly
technical_requirements.description: No new table, dashboard, stage, or agent. No change to belt ranking beyond the existing dispatch reading whatever criticality/verdict fields already exist. Deleting ventures or creating the clean-slate test venture itself (that is ratification 3c4a6781's own execution, a separate future chairman-approved SD once FR-6 surfaces the decision). Re-triaging items already inside the 58cc4231 baseline (they ride to completion under their existing SD/QF workflow, untouched by this gate).

test_scenarios.scenario: FR-1 QF gate, flag OFF, no --criticality
FR-1 QF gate, flag ON, no --criticality
test_scenarios.expected: Non-zero exit, no insert, four criteria named
No quick_fixes insert; routes via FR-3

test_scenarios.expected: emitFeedback called with category=harness_backlog, printed output names the feedback row id
generateRemediationSD spawns --criticality later; insertDraftRemediationSd and mintVentureQuickFix always stamp metadata.criticality='later'

BASELINE_REMAINING sd=N qf=M matches an independent direct query; recomputed sha256 matches the stored historical value using the confirmed algorithm; fails loud on simulated tampering; never writes to the feedback table
First sd=0/qf=0 run creates one chairman_decisions row; second run creates none; sd>0 or qf>0 never calls recordPendingDecision

acceptance_criteria: A create-quick-fix.js call without a criticality verdict is refused (once QF_CRITICALITY_GATE_ENFORCE is flipped on) with the four criteria named; with 'later' it lands a harness_backlog feedback row and no quick_fixes row; with 'critical' it files normally with the verdict and reason on the row.
The same three behaviors hold for the SD creation path via createSD().

All direct-insert bypass paths (insertSDIdempotent as the primary/highest-volume target, plus insertDraftRemediationSd, mintVentureQuickFix, and the dormant line-1487 venture-expansion insert) always carry an explicit metadata.criticality='later' stamp, never silently uncategorized.

The baseline reader prints BASELINE_REMAINING with counts that match a direct query over the 58cc4231 id lists, and fails loud if the recomputed sha256 (using the confirmed original algorithm) does not match the stored historical value.
At sd=0 qf=0 the reader creates exactly one chairman decision row referencing 3c4a6781, and a second run creates none.
Unit tests cover each behavior, run in the standard test suite.

risks.risk: Filers route real problems to 'later' to avoid work
risks.mitigation: Every 'later' verdict carries a mandatory one-line reason on an auditable feedback row; a future SD can build a periodic review of the later-routed list (out of scope here).

risks.risk: Bulk generator/bridge paths (lifecycle-sd-bridge.js, sd-generator.js) firing in volume
risks.mitigation: Every direct-insert bypass path defaults to 'later', keeping them off the belt without dropping their findings -- explicitly never defaulting to 'critical' under any circumstance.

risks.risk: The 4 already-live programmatic createSD() callers (FR-2) or the lifecycle-sd-bridge.js bypass (FR-4) break when their respective flags flip to enforced, if any call site is missed
risks.mitigation: Each named call site gets an explicit, grep-testable criticality:'later' stamp in this SD itself (not deferred to flag-flip time); the retrospective at PLAN-TO-LEAD names any further static call sites found during EXEC that were deliberately deferred, so none are silently dropped.

consumers: Every worker/Adam-seat filing a QF or SD via create-quick-fix.js or leo-create-sd.js's 8 CLI lanes
Adam's quiet tick and plan check (consume BASELINE_REMAINING)
dependencies: feedback row 58cc4231 (read, and one new metadata key added)
data_contracts: feedback table is read-only for this SD -- no new keys, no writes (immutability trigger)
observability_rollout: Warn-first release: both flags OFF, every ungated filing logs a distinguishable warning naming the flag it would have enforced. A future SD flips both flags to true once filers have had one release cycle to adopt --criticality, per the SD's own 'warn-first for one release, then enforce' text.

system_architecture.summary: 4 existing files gain a criticality check at their real creation choke points (2 CLI tools, 2 direct-insert bypass functions); 1 new reader script surfaces baseline-remaining counts and, once, the finish-line chairman decision; 2 new leo_feature_flags rows govern the warn-first rollout.
